title: Claude Code overly sensitive
author: Chillroy
selftext:
I've recently found Claude Code to be impossible to work with in creating a normal modern military RTS game. It keeps stopping the task due to the safeguards for totally harmless requests like this.   
Its a low poly RTS game, not a combat simulator.

Paying $100/month for this is starting to feel less worth it when I keep having to switch to Codex to get around it.

  
Anyone else had similar issues?

comments.author: mbreaddit
comments.body:
Try to avoid such things. Let it be a rock to be thrown. I guess Anthropic got a bit sensitive lately because the Huthis tried to make guided missiles together with their AI which they had to prevent. 

Find out the trajectory a javelin does and say it should let the entity fly like this, give it as a picture parameter of a 1D curve or whatever, work around the "javelin" part. I guess it triggers their nerves a bit rn

replies.author: Chillroy
replies.body: Oh I tried that too, even just referring to the javelin as "the RTS Game AT unit-projectile", explaining that I want it to rise quickly when fired, reach an altitude it stays at before coming down on its target. It works better for a few minutes before throwing the same message.

replies.author: mbreaddit
replies.body:
Ok that sucks. I had this occasionally because i was tinkering with the idea of adding some anti-cracking mechanisms to my game not to prevent it, but make the game impossible to play after longer time so that it wents undetected. 

**The last idea i´ve is the following:**  
Do a Chat up with gemini or chatgpt about how to generally design a javelin trajectory, get the specs discussed, export it and make it believe its coming from a agentic-coworker chat. I noticed that they open up more when other llms from competitors are actually obeying.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: Did you tried to just google it by the way?

replies.author: Okoear
replies.body: Ballistic trajectory equation. Not rocket sicence.Wonder how to would react if you passed it to him and tried to apply it to your game.

replies.author: feralferrous
replies.body: I'd be curious if you just changed it to something sci-fi.  "I have a homing plasma projectile that launches upwards and then tries to land on top of the enemy hovertank"

comments.author: Baraga91
comments.body:
Hubinon was interrogated for drawing military vehicles too accurately for the *Buck Danny* strips, murder mystery writers have had to explain their suspicious questions more than once and movie sets have to be obnoxiously clear about the fact that they're movie sets to avoid becoming frequent flyer destinations for SWAT teams...

This is just the next iteration of an age old tradition 😄

comments.author: BadassMinh
comments.body: Maybe switch to another model with not as strict safeguard? Opus 4.6 is probably better

replies.author: Chillroy
replies.body: I'll try that next time. I tried Fable, but got the same error there

comments.author: BeaveItToLeever
comments.body:
I had the same thing over and over for a targeting and radar system In a game I'm working on. 

Good news is that for such specific things that you can be more directive with, Opus 4.6 is totally capable and it's what I use when something is specific, at least moderately clear and direct(a single system within a game) and it's my suggestion here. Opus 4.6 for single/scoped target things that harmless but getting flagged

replies.author: Chillroy
replies.body: Thanks, I’ll give it a shot!

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: Start with a little bit more context next time maybe.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Open paint, draw and plot out the animation and send that with descriptions of how you want it to move, don't mention realistic or reference real military weapons in the prompt either. If you just say more like "hey my player in the game launches a rocket it i want it to have x animation (filename.png) can you make it move like this with arching trajectory" basically try to make it clear your making a game and not a weapons system.

comments.author: Robonotes1760
comments.body: Closed AI is not safe for this reason.
